Guidance & outlook: Real GDP growth was estimated at 7.7% during the year, following growth rates of 7.1% in FY 2024-25 and 7.2% in FY 2023-24.

CPI inﬂation remained largely within the target range, while the Reserve Bank of India maintained the repo rate at 5.25% with a supportive policy stance to ensure adequate liquidity and growth momentum.

The Union Budget 2026-27 further reinforced the government's emphasis on infrastructure-led growth, with public capital expenditure increased to `12.2 lakh crore from `11.2 lakh crore in FY 2025-26, alongside continued investments in logistics, 2industrial corridors, energy security and strategic manufacturing sectors .
Growth & demand: Real GDP growth was estimated at 7.7%, driven by resilient consumption, healthy investment momentum and improving industrial output.

Global GDP growth stood at 3.4%, supported by steady momentum across Emerging Market and Developing Economies (EMDEs), stronger export activity and improving investments across industrial and infrastructure sectors, while advanced economies grew by 1.9%.
Total textile exports, including handicrafts, increased by 2.1% to `3.16 lakh crore, supported by growth across readymade garments, 5man-made textiles and value-added product categories.
Margins & costs: The Company experienced a decline in the performance as compared to previous years, primarily due to a signiﬁcant increase in the cost of raw materials, power and fuel, and logistics and other costs.
Many segments, particularly spinning and processing, suﬀer from technological obsolescence, which leads to higher production costs and reduced competitiveness-especially against low-cost imports.
Moreover, the sector is vulnerable to input cost volatility, particularly in the pricing of raw materials like cotton, which directly impacts proﬁtability and pricing ﬂexibility.
